# v3.03-dev

Scheduled-export credentials are now checked when you save them, and mail servers
have to prove who they are.

**If you email scheduled reports through a server with a self-signed certificate,
read Upgrading — this release needs one change from you.**

## Changed

- **Training Tracker now verifies your mail server's certificate before handing
  over the SMTP password.** It previously accepted any certificate from any
  server, so the password could be handed to something that had taken the mail
  server's place on the network.

  There is a new **Allow self-signed certificate** tickbox on the SMTP credential
  for installations that need it. See Upgrading.

## Fixed

- **Provider credentials are validated when you save them.** The SMTP host must
  be a hostname or an IP address and the port a number between 1 and 65535, so a
  typo is reported there and then instead of surfacing days later as a report
  that never arrived.

- **Only the settings a provider actually uses can be stored.** Anything else is
  refused rather than quietly kept alongside the real settings.

- **The OneDrive tenant ID is checked against a strict format.** It could
  previously contain characters that reshaped the sign-in request, sending it
  somewhere other than the intended address within the sign-in service.

- **Saving a credential now tells you what was wrong**, instead of the same
  "failed to save" message whatever the cause. A malformed request is reported
  as such rather than as a server error.

- **Emailing a scheduled report now gives up after a few seconds** when the mail
  server cannot be reached, rather than waiting around two minutes on every
  attempt. The connection test already behaved this way; sending did not.

## Upgrading

**Only if you email scheduled reports through a server with a self-signed or
otherwise untrusted certificate.** Certificate checking used to be off for
everyone, so such an installation needs one change after this update.

The symptom is scheduled mail stopping, with the error *"Could not connect to the
configured host and port"*. Either install a trusted certificate on the mail
server, or go to **Admin → Scheduled Exports**, edit the SMTP credential, tick
**Allow self-signed certificate**, and save.

Nothing else needs action. Credentials already saved keep working, and are
re-checked the next time you edit and save one.
